Now plus later

A return is the next reward plus everything after it, discounted once. Average that over what can happen next and you get the core of every value method: a state's value is the expected next reward plus the discounted value of the state you land in.

A return, computed backwards

Sample an episode on the icy grid (Lesson 20's arrows, ε = 0.2), then fill in the returns from the end. Each $G_t$ needs only the reward after it and the $G_{t+1}$ below it.

The maths

Pull the first reward out of the return:

$$\begin{aligned} G_t &= R_{t+1} + \gamma R_{t+2} + \gamma^2 R_{t+3} + \dots \\ &= R_{t+1} + \gamma\big(R_{t+2} + \gamma R_{t+3} + \dots\big) \\ &= R_{t+1} + \gamma\, G_{t+1} \end{aligned}$$

With $G_T = 0$ at the end of an episode, this computes every return in one backward pass. That is the table above.

Now take expectations. Given $S_t = s$, the expected $G_{t+1}$ depends on where the agent lands. Given it lands in $s'$, the Markov property (Lesson 15) says the future looks the same as starting in $s'$, so that expectation is $v_\pi(s')$:

$$\begin{aligned} v_\pi(s) &= \mathbb{E}_\pi[R_{t+1} + \gamma G_{t+1} \mid S_t = s] \\ &= \mathbb{E}_\pi[R_{t+1} + \gamma\, v_\pi(S_{t+1}) \mid S_t = s] \end{aligned}$$

Value now equals expected reward now plus discounted value later. In the bar above, green is $\mathbb{E}[R_{t+1}]$ and blue is $\gamma\,\mathbb{E}[v_\pi(S_{t+1})]$.

This is a statement about $v_\pi$ itself: every state's value is tied to its neighbours' values. Lesson 26 writes the expectation out in full, and Lesson 45 learns from it one sample at a time.
